parts.text:
4
A student wishes to measure a distance of about 10 cm to a precision of 0.01 cm.
Which measuring instrument should be used?
A
metre rule
B
micrometer
C
tape measure
D
vernier calipers

hints: Notice the two numbers in the stem: length about $10\text{ cm}$ and required precision $0.01\text{ cm}$, which is $0.1\text{ mm}$.
Recall the typical smallest division for each tool: metre rule and tape measure to $0.1\text{ cm}$, vernier calipers to $0.01\text{ cm}$, micrometer to $0.001\text{ cm}$.
Now check range as well as precision - which tool with $0.01\text{ cm}$ precision can still open wide enough to measure $10\text{ cm}$?
walkthrough: Identify what is needed: measure $L \approx 10\text{ cm}$ with smallest readable change of $0.01\text{ cm}$.
Recall precisions: metre rule $\approx 0.1\text{ cm}$, tape measure $\approx 0.1\text{ cm}$, vernier calipers $\approx 0.01\text{ cm}$, micrometer $\approx 0.001\text{ cm}$.
Eliminate metre rule and tape measure because $0.1\text{ cm} > 0.01\text{ cm}$, so they are not precise enough.
Compare the two precise tools on range: a standard micrometer measures only small objects up to about $2.5\text{ cm}$, while vernier calipers measure up to about $10-15\text{ cm}$.
Since $10\text{ cm}$ is within the calipers range and matches its $0.01\text{ cm}$ precision, the suitable instrument is vernier calipers. This is option D

A.explanation: A metre rule typically reads to $0.1\text{ cm}$, which is ten times too coarse for the required $0.01\text{ cm}$ precision.

B.explanation: A micrometer reads to $0.001\text{ cm}$ but its range is usually only about $2.5\text{ cm}$, so it cannot span a distance of about $10\text{ cm}$.

C.explanation: A tape measure typically reads to $0.1\text{ cm}$ at best and is for longer distances, so it cannot give $0.01\text{ cm}$ precision.

D.explanation: Vernier calipers read to $0.01\text{ cm}$ and have a range over $10\text{ cm}$, matching both the size and precision required.
